methodological_rigor.justification: NORSE is a randomized noncomparative phase II trial (n=87 treated) with 1:1 random assignment stratified by ECOG PS and a prespecified noncomparative sample-size rationale (excluding ORR thresholds of 30% and 40%). The design is appropriate for precision-of-estimation goals but, as the authors acknowledge, was underpowered even for these thresholds (actual n=43/44 instead of 45 per arm). Central or local FGFR testing was used with retrospective central confirmation. Key limitations: no formal between-arm comparison, short follow-up, absence of control arm, and standard of care evolved (enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab) during the study.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Erdafitinib is approved in the post-platinum setting on the basis of THOR; NORSE provides first-line activity data in a biomarker-selected cisplatin-ineligible population with manageable safety and encouraging ORR (44.2% and 54.5%). However, the first-line standard of care has shifted to enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, limiting immediate practice impact. Single-arm-equivalent phase II cohort -> Oxford LoE 2b.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript includes a CONSORT-style flow diagram, detailed eligibility, treatment schedule with uptitration rules, AE grading per CTCAE v5.0, and explicit noncomparative statistical plan. Randomization and stratification are described; long-term extension phase is transparent. Data-availability statement not visible in normalized text; Data Supplement referenced but not inspected.

novelty_literature.justification: NORSE extends erdafitinib to the first-line cisplatin-ineligible FGFR-altered mUC setting and explores combination with cetrelimab. The erdafitinib monotherapy signal is consistent with THOR and prior phase II work (ORR 40-46%). The cetrelimab combination data (ORR 54.5%, 6 CRs) is a modest but meaningful addition. Not a novel class; extends known agents to a new line of therapy.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with explicit primary/secondary endpoints, clear efficacy tables, and candid acknowledgement of limitations including the shifting standard of care. Subgroup analyses are framed as hypothesis-generating. Safety reporting is thorough, especially for AEs of interest (hyperphosphatemia, central serous retinopathy, immune-related AEs).

key_strengths: First dedicated biomarker-selected first-line study of erdafitinib +/- PD-1 inhibition in cisplatin-ineligible mUC
Encouraging ORR (44.2% erdafitinib; 54.5% combination) with durable responses (6 CRs in combination arm)
Safety profile consistent with each individual agent; no additive toxicity with cetrelimab
Transparent noncomparative statistical design and explicit acknowledgement of shifting standard of care
key_concerns: Noncomparative design and modest sample size preclude between-arm inference
Follow-up short (median 14.2 months); OS and DOR CIs wide (median DOR NE in CR responders)
SOC has evolved to enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab, limiting current practice impact
Central serous retinopathy in ~20% highlights ongoing toxicity concerns
Subgroup analyses (PD-L1, FGFR alteration type) are hypothesis-generating only
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent, well-reported phase II study with biomarker-selected population and clinically meaningful activity but incremental value given evolved SOC and lack of comparative inference; Tier 2 (e.g., JCO Precision Oncology/ESMO Open) is appropriate.
